subject: Breakglass: BoltStream live throughput collapse after client SDK update
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@boltstream.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: production sess/throughput collapse after bolt-js 1.4.2 rollout

Soojin —

We started a staged rollout of bolt-js 1.4.2 to our live checkout in us-west at ~08:55 PT and within ~5 minutes we saw a surge of stream disconnects and 5xx error spikes. Throughput to Redwood endpoints dropped ~60% on our busiest shard and customer-facing latency p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~2.3s.

We rolled the client back to 1.4.1 and the traffic mostly recovered after 10m, but this hit many customers and triggered our incident hotline. Attaching the snippet of error logs and a screenshot of the live dashboard.

Key details:
- SDK: bolt-js 1.4.2 (we updated via CDN)
- Affected endpoints: /v1/live/generate (streaming)
- Symptoms: early connection closes, 502/ERR_STREAM_ABORT, malformed response headers seen in client logs (see attachment).

We need immediate help: is there anything in your runtime that changed parsing expectations? We can provide additional logs and reproduce in a staging cluster if you want.

—Alex
Alex Kim
Site Reliability Lead | BoltStream
attachments: bolt-error-logs.txt, bolt-error-screenshot.png

- Is the rollback fully completed for all clients? If any regions are still on 1.4.2, let us know and we’ll route around them.

We’re treating this as breakglass. Sean — can you take a look at runtime logs for the region and check for dechunker/header parsing anomalies? Rishi — I’ll coordinate customer comms and the short-term mitigation.

We’ll aim to get a plan within an hour.

—Soojin

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@boltstream.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: production sess/throughput collapse after bolt-js 1.4.2 rollout

Team / Alex —

Quick technical triage notes from runtime/SRE: we observed repeated instances where streaming frames contained header lines split across TCP segment boundaries and our dechunker in the streaming gateway interpreted a trailing CR as end-of-headers in a subset of sequences. This manifests as truncated pseudo-headers on the server and then a mismatch when the client attempts to read the continuation, leading to an early stream abort (ERR_STREAM_ABORT) or a 502.

Representative log excerpt (timestamped):
[2026-04-05T08:57:12.345Z] shard-7 conn=0x7fa2 parse: got chunk: "content-type: application/grpc+json
content-length: 128
user-agent: bolt-js/1.4.2
trace-id: ..."
[2026-04-05T08:57:12.346Z] shard-7 conn=0x7fa2 parse: next chunk: "
accept-encoding: gzip
..."
[2026-04-05T08:57:12.346Z] shard-7 conn=0x7fa2 dechunker: saw lone CR, treating as terminator in fast-path (BUG)
[2026-04-05T08:57:12.347Z] shard-7 conn=0x7fa2 stream: frame parse failed -> closing with ERR_STREAM_ABORT (client side sees truncated headers)

Root cause hypothesis: the bolt-js 1.4.2 emitter changes framing such that some header lines are split on CR/LF boundaries in ways our fast-path did not expect. The gating condition appears on hosts using TCP segmentation offload combined with HTTP/2 flow bursts.

Mitigation plan (high confidence):
1) Build/validate a runtime hotfix removing the fast-path CR-as-terminator shortcut and falling back to the safe full-scan header assembly. (Jira: INF-8932)
2) Roll the hotfix to staging and run the bolt-js 1.4.2 reproduction harness (we already have a failing unit test).
3) If pass, deploy to us-west only initially with traffic mirroring for 30m, then incrementally increase.
4) Add a short-term temporary ACL that routes traffic from known bolt-js 1.4.2 user-agents to a compatibility proxy that performs robust reassembly (if hotfix will take longer).

Estimated ETA for a hotfix build + staging run: 2.5 hours. ETA for canary deploy (us-west) if tests pass: +1 hour.

I’ll file a postmortem template and capture logs. Linking to the internal jira and a perf snapshot: https://redwood.internal/jira/INF-8932 and https://dashboard.redwood.com/r/boltstream/throughput?from=2026-04-05T08:30Z.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal SRE, Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: URGENT: production sess/throughput collapse after bolt-js 1.4.2 rollout

Alex —

Quick summary and next steps for customers and BoltStream operators:

What happened (short): bolt-js 1.4.2 introduced framing patterns that exposed a dechunker fast-path bug in our streaming gateway. That caused header fragmentation to be misinterpreted and led to stream aborts and elevated error rates.

Immediate customer-facing actions (we recommend):
- If you haven’t fully rolled back, pin to bolt-js 1.4.1 (recommended immediate rollback).
- If rollback is not possible for any reason, toggle your client to disable HTTP/2 fast-start (we can provide exact flag names) and avoid CDN-inflicted segmentation for the moment.

Our commitments:
- Engineering (Sean) will push a hotfix to staging within ~2.5 hours and run your 1.4.2 reproduction.
- If tests pass, we will canary to us-west in a controlled rollout and provide minute-by-minute observability.
- CS (Rishi) will prepare incident communications and a short customer credit proposal; Marissa will confirm approvals for the largest impacted accounts.
- We’ll produce a postmortem with timeline and remediation items within 72 hours.

Alex, does that plan work for you? If you want, we can also set an emergency bridge now (please share a dial-in) — we’re standing by.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive (Strategic Accounts) | Redwood Inference
